news.title: Transshipment Crackdowns Won’t Fix the U.S.-China Trade Imbalance
news.summary_en: The White House alleges that Chinese exports are being rerouted through third countries to circumvent U.S. tariffs. By analyzing transshipment activity and substantive supply chain shifts, CSIS challenges this diagnosis and highlights persistent structural issues.

news.title: Fast Following: Military Emulation and Twenty-First-Century Transformation
news.summary_en: Modern war is a contest of learning and adaptation, and the lessons travel in a matter of weeks. Fast following, or copying, improving, and fielding proven innovations at speed, is now a core competency, yet Western militaries remain slow to build it.

news.title: FY 2027 Defense Funding: Potential Post-Midterm Outcomes
news.summary_en: Congress has a full post-midterm agenda, with action needed to fund the Department of Defense and federal government and reconciliation legislation to consider. Seamus Daniels lays out the factors that will shape FY 2027 defense funding decisions after the midterms.

news.title: Decoding the Right-to-Repair Debate
news.summary_en: The right-to-repair debate, concerning who controls U.S. defense IP, has become a contentious issue in defense acquisition policy. Lawmakers need to balance the military’s push for greater access to technical data and industry’s fear of losing revenue and IP control.

news.title: Business Support for Human Rights Defenders in an Era of Government Retrenchment
news.summary_en: Human rights defenders are vital partners for businesses operating around the globe. Civic space and the business operating environment are fundamentally intertwined. Businesses should, can, and have supported HRDs in their important work, and such support is more needed than ever.
